metais grep — Search a package's entries for a regular expression, with context.

Usage:
  metais grep <package> <pattern> [<glob>]... [--context <n> | -C <n>]
              [--ignore-case | -i] [--max-results <n>]
              [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

The pattern is RE2 syntax, as Go's regexp defines it, and is matched against
each line without its line ending, so ^ and $ anchor the line; a CR before the
LF is part of the ending. --ignore-case prepends (?i). The pattern is bounded by
the pattern-length, regex-program and regex-work limits.

Globs select the entries searched (metais help globs); with none, every entry is
searched but those beneath a segment that begins with a dot, so .compiled/ is
searched only when a glob names it. Entries are searched in path order, lines in
order. Binary entries are skipped and listed.

--max-results bounds the matching lines reported, from 1 to the grep-matches
limit; the search still runs to the end, and counts every matching line. A line
longer than 1024 bytes is shown cut, and read --lines gives it whole. No match
is not a failure: grep exits 0.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a
      package is read with random access. Required.
  <pattern>
      A regular expression in RE2 syntax; write -- before one that begins with
      -. Required.
  <glob>
      A glob selecting the entries to search; every entry when none is given.

Flags:
  -C, --context <n>
      Show n lines before and after each matching line, from 0 to the
      grep-context limit. Default: 0.
  -i, --ignore-case
      Match letters regardless of case.
  --max-results <n>
      Report at most n matching lines, from 1 to the grep-matches limit; by
      default 100, or the limit when it is lower. Default: 100.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  Each matching line as path:line:text and each line of context as
  path-line-text, with -- between groups that are not adjacent; a truncation
  notice and the binary entries skipped go to standard error. With --json, one
  metais.grep/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits
  usage.bad_glob
      A glob does not satisfy the glob grammar.
      Next: metais help globs
  usage.bad_pattern
      The pattern is not RE2 syntax, or breaches pattern-length, regex-program
      or regex-work.
      Next: metais limits
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais grep --help
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais grep --help
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais grep --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais grep --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais grep --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais grep --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals grep' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  manifest.* (60)  The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
  package.* (46)   The package is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (10)    An input schema is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  template.* (9)   An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>

Examples:
  metais grep report-1.0.0.metais 'alt text' references/
      Searches the references.
  metais grep report-1.0.0.metais -i -C 2 '^## ' '**/*.md'
      Lists every level-2 heading of the Markdown entries, with two lines around
      each.
  metais grep report-1.0.0.metais schema .compiled/** --json
      Searches the compiled files, as one metais.grep/1 document.
